messages:
Maria: Quick note: building on the quota RFC, I prototyped a decoupled admission flow that separates provisional "lease" tokens from committed accounting and folds per-tenant abuse scores into the real-time admission decision. Wanted quick feedback on contract surface and safety tradeoffs.
Cheng: TL;DR bullets pls, what's the main behavioral change vs today?
Maria: Today: router asks quota service for hard tokens -> admission is binary. New: router sends an admission hint (nominal tokens + context). Admission service returns typed outcomes: accept / accept-probabilistic / reject / degrade-to-best-effort. Abuse score changes probabilistic thresholds and provisional caps.
Oliver: So router gets simpler but admission becomes stateful and performance sensitive. How do we keep tail latency stable for hot tenants?
Maria: Two main mitigations: 1) local tenant profile cache in router for hot-path fast heuristics (TTL+version), 2) optimistic local provisional decrements with async reconcile to authoritative counters. Fast-path admits use cached decision; reconciler fixes drift.
Hannah: Async optimistic admits sound risky for accounting and fairness. How do you prevent quota drift or double-charging?
Maria: Keep two counters per tenant: "committed_tokens" (source of truth) and "provisional_tokens" (local). Router deducts provisional immediately. Background reconciler batches provisional -> commit via idempotent ledger updates. If reconcile finds an overage we emit compensating metrics and open a short soft-shed window.
Kumar: Failure modes? If reconciler lags or is down what should admission do?
Maria: Failure modes + responses: 1) slow reconciler: adaptively shrink provisional caps per-tenant to keep provisional/committed ratio under threshold; 2) reconciler outage: fallback to conservative sync path (strict token check); 3) abusive tenant: cap provisional based on abuse-score and feature-flag disable for sensitive customers.
Cheng: API sketch between router -> admission look like: ```POST /admit { tenant_id, model, seq_len, hint_tokens, hint_version } => { decision: "accept" | "probabilistic" | "reject" | "degrade", mode: "sync" | "async", token_charge: number, degrade_hint: string|null, soft_window_s: number, reason_code: string, trace_id: string }``` Add separate batch accounting endpoint for reconciliation.
Oliver: Add an explicit "hint_version" so we can evolve heuristics. Also include a cheap decision latency budget in the response so router can route to sync path if admission is slow.
Hannah: Abuse-score integration: we must avoid flapping when scores change. Propose smoothed score + action hysteresis.
Maria: Agreed. Proposal: abuse_score_smoothed = EMA(abuse_score, alpha=0.2); thresholds map to actions: warn, throttle, probation, evict. Stored in config so ops can tune without deploy.
Kumar: Testing plan? Need robust attack sims and chaos for reconciler issues. Also model fallback options instead of outright reject.
Maria: Test plan outline: - Offline sim with 50k synthetic tenants (mix honest vs abusive) - Chaos runs forcing reconciler lag and packet loss - Canary rollout (1% traffic) feature-flagged per org + region - Add metrics: provisional/committed ratio, reconcile lag histogram, tenant-overage events, per-tenant provisional cap hits. Alert if provisional/committed > 0.15 for >5m.
Cheng: Also provide a "degrade_hint" in admission response so router can transparently pick a cheaper or quantized model instead of rejecting. Example: {"decision":"probabilistic","token_charge":3,"degrade_hint":"gptj-quant-v0.9","soft_window_s":30}.
Oliver: On fairness: admission should handle micro fairness (per-second / minute), but keep a global planner for long-term fairness weights and rebalances (daily/weekly). Planner updates admission profiles periodically.
Hannah: For Private deployments and KMS boundaries: are we shipping abuse scores outside customer VPC? Privacy reqs?
Maria: Keep scores in control plane. For VPC/on-prem, admission fetches scores via vetted mTLS call inside customer network. Offer a local-abuse-plugin hook for air-gapped installs. Document in security playbook.
Kumar: Add a per-org feature flag to disable provisional mode for compliance customers.
Maria: Done. Also adding reconciliation safety knobs: idempotent batch tokens, monotonic sequence per-tenant, and compensating metrics/events if we hit overage.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag created: admission-provisional-v1 on staging.
Maria: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with API schema, reconciliation design, failure modes, rollout checklist, and test harness configs. Who wants to co-author? :raised_hands:
Cheng: I'll co-author API schema + latency budget notes.
Oliver: I'll prototype reconciler batching heuristics and backoff strategies.
Hannah: I'll cover security/privacy and ops guardrails.
Kumar: I'll develop attack scenarios and synthetic load configs.
Maria: Thanks all, will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
